thread:
maria: Heads-up — we're onboarding a new GPU fleet in eu-west-1 for inference. Need advice on VPCE + NLB target quotas across accounts. Planning cross-account PrivateLink for model serving. Can we reuse existing VPCEs or do we need new ones?
ben: How many targets/endpoints are we expecting? AZs? account IDs?
maria: Rough numbers: ~1200 NLB targets total (we expect ~300 concurrent nodes per AZ x 4 AZs), 8 interface endpoints (PrivateLink) per customer account, and we'll support ~10 customer accounts initially. So potentially ~80 interface endpoints attached to our VPC service.
alex: Ok. A few notes: AWS defaults are low for some of these — interface endpoints per VPC often default to 50, targets per target group default 1000. Cross-account VPCE service attachments can hit region-wide limits for NLB targets / target groups.
ben: Right — target groups per NLB + targets per TG matter. If a single target group tops at 1000 targets, we may need to shard across 2 TGs. Sharding means more target group ARNs and more target registrations. That can trigger other quotas (target group attachments, rules).
maria: Sharding sounds fine. What about reusing VPCEs? I was hoping to avoid opening 10x VPCEs per customer.
alex: You can reuse a single VPC endpoint service (NLB as the service) and allow multiple principal accounts to create VPCEs pointing to it. But each VPCE is a managed endpoint in the customer's VPC — so you still get one interface endpoint object per customer per AZ. That counts against the customer's endpoint quota and your service's permissions. For high fanout, you often hit the "Interface endpoints per NLB" / "VPCE attachments" soft limits.
devx: From a DX POV, fewer endpoints is simpler. Two approaches we've used: 1) central shared VPCE in a connectivity VPC + Transit/privatelink routing (adds networking complexity), or 2) accept one interface endpoint per customer and proactively request quota increases. Option 1 reduces number of VPCE objects but requires cross-VPC routing (Transit Gateway or routing through peering).
ben: Operational ask: we should create an AWS support quota case for: (a) Interface endpoints per region -> bump from 50 -> 500, (b) Targets per target group -> bump from 1000 -> 2000, (c) Target groups per NLB -> bump from default -> 20 (example). Also confirm cross-account VPCE attachments limit with account team.
maria: I'll submit the quota case. Any suggested text for the request?
alex: Copy/paste this for the support case: 
```
We are launching a GPU inference fleet (model-serving NLB) in eu-west-1 using AWS PrivateLink for cross-account access. Expected scale: ~1200 targets across 4 AZs and up to 80 interface endpoints (one per customer account per AZ). Please increase the following quotas in eu-west-1 for account 123456789012: Interface endpoints per VPC -> 500, Targets per target group -> 2000, Target groups per load balancer -> 50. We also request guidance on soft limits related to cross-account VPCE attachments for high fanout PrivateLink services.
```
maria: Nice, thanks. I'll paste that in the quota form.
devx: Also include the architecture doc link and a short timeline (we're targeting end of quarter). Helps expedite. :rocket:
ben: FYI — if AWS pushes back, fallback plan is split the fleet into region+account specific NLBs and use a lightweight ingress proxy to reduce number of targets per NLB. That increases cost but avoids quota waits.
sre-bot: quota-ticket-created: AWS Support case 987654321 opened for eu-west-1 quota increases. ETA: TBD.
maria: Thanks all — I'll tag infra-owners and add the runbook link here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpce-nlb-scale. I'll update when support responds. :white_check_mark:
